name: io-uring-setup
why: io_uring_setup creates a ring a syscall-hooking sensor may not see; ring creation by a non-allowlisted process is the anchor
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for io_uring_bypass_behavioral.c's io_uring_setup(8, &params) record; a0=8 entries, a1=params ptr, exit is the decimal ring fd (3)

name: io-uring-enter-only
why: io_uring_enter submits and reaps on an existing ring, once per I/O batch; the rule keys on ring creation only, so an enter keeps the io_uring surface but is not the setup, and flipping only the syscall name to io_uring_setup fires
source: synthetic: a process issuing io_uring_enter (the OR's second block); a0=ring fd, a1=to_submit

name: fio-ioctl-not-ring
why: fio also issues ordinary block-device ioctls (BLKGETSIZE64) rather than submitting through its ring; an audited ioctl keeps the SYSCALL surface but is neither ring syscall, so flipping the syscall name to either anchored ring call fires. (io_uring_register, the real non-setup/non-enter ring op, is NOT in detections/audit/atomic.rules, so it can never reach this pipeline -- an audited look-alike is used instead.)
source: synthetic: fio querying the target block device with ioctl; ioctl is audited, io_uring_register is not

name: splice-not-ring
why: splice() is the classic zero-copy path a server uses instead of an io_uring ring; it is audited and keeps the SYSCALL surface but is neither ring syscall, so flipping the syscall name to either anchored ring call fires. (read(), the syscall io_uring most directly replaces, is NOT audited by atomic.rules, so an audited data-movement look-alike is used instead.)
source: synthetic: a server moving data with splice() rather than a ring; splice is audited, read is not

name: fio-io-uring-enter-batch
why: fio --ioengine=io_uring calls io_uring_enter for every submit-and-wait batch on its ring; the old rule fired on each one (57,887 hits in one CI capture). The rule keys on ring creation only, so a per-batch enter must not fire
source: benign corpus template 'fio io_uring_enter (submit + wait)'; io_uring_enter(2) man page

name: io-uring-setup-sqpoll-agent
why: an implant that does its file and network I/O through io_uring must create its ring first; a ring created with IORING_SETUP_SQPOLL (flags in the params struct, a1 a pointer) by a non-baselined binary fires at the setup
source: synthetic: io_uring_setup(64 entries, &params) as in io_uring_setup(2); the ring-only I/O model of io_uring-based implants
